title: Curves over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A *geometrically integral smooth projective curve over $k$* is a smooth projective curve $C$ over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] (in particular of dimension exactly $1$), which is geometrically integral over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Its *genus* is
$$g(C):=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},$$
where $H^1$ denotes cohomology of the structure sheaf as an $\mathcal O_C$-module [pqf-def-cohomology] and dimension is as in [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This cohomology group is finite-dimensional.

For every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $C_K=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then $C_K$ is again a geometrically integral smooth projective curve over $K$ and $g(C_K)=g(C)$.

If $K$ is algebraically closed, $C_K$ is a proper smooth connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-curves], and its genus of [def-sc-genus] equals $g(C)$. Thus the degree and $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ conventions of [def-sc-pic0] apply to $C_K$.

proof.text: The dimension-one condition makes $C$ a curve in [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. Geometric integrality implies geometric irreducibility: for each field extension the resulting integral scheme is irreducible, by the equivalent characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme] and the definitions in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Hence [lem-pc-genus-well-defined] applies over the arbitrary field $k$ and gives $\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)<\infty$. This defines a finite nonnegative integer genus.

source.place: First sentence: finiteness of the genus; the dimension-one hypothesis is restored from the unit and def-pc-smooth-projective-curve.

proof.text: Fix a field extension $K/k$, and write $p:C_K\to C$ for the projection. The structure morphism of $C$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. The $k$-module $K$ is free on a vector-space basis, so tensoring with $K$ is a direct sum of copies of the identity functor and preserves injections; thus $K$ is flat over $k$. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent: on any affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is the module sheaf associated to $A$, as in [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] with $X=C$, $k'=K$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$, and $i=1$. It gives the canonical $K$-linear isomorphism $H^1(C_K,p^*\mathcal O_C)\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\otimes_kK$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, affine-base formula (2); blueprint proof, second sentence.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] for $p$, the canonical morphism $p^*\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_{C_K}$ is an isomorphism. Applying the cohomology functor [pqf-def-cohomology] to it in degree $1$ and combining with step 2 gives $H^1(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\otimes_kK$. These are $K$-linear identifications, with scalar action on the tensor factor $K$. Swapping tensor factors and applying [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] to the finite-dimensional space from step 1 proves $\dim_KH^1(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, and finiteness on the left.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2), with the pullback of the structure sheaf and the dimension of scalar extension made explicit.

proof.text: Smoothness of $C_K/K$ follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and projectivity from [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Its dimension is $1$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change], applied to the curve $C/k$. By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $C_K$ is integral. Its structure morphism is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper] and [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. These are all the conditions of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] over $K$.

source.place: The phrase g(C_K) in the arbitrary-field-extension assertion requires verifying that C_K is a curve of the same kind.

proof.text: For any further field extension $L/K$, the iterated base change $(C_K)_L$ identifies with $C_L$: both fibre products have the universal property of $C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ ([def-pc-base-change]). The composite $k\to K\to L$ is a field extension, so $C_L$ is integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Thus $C_K$ is geometrically integral over $K$. Together with step 4 this makes its genus defined by the displayed formula, and step 3 gives $g(C_K)=g(C)$.

source.place: Arbitrary field extensions: stability of geometric integrality and the meaning of g(C_K).

proof.text: If $K$ is algebraically closed, apply [lem-pc-curves-are-sc] to the smooth projective curve $C_K/K$ of step 4. It is a smooth connected curve in the conventions of [def-sc-curves], and it is proper by step 4. The definition [def-sc-genus] is precisely $\dim_KH^1(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K})$, which equals $g(C)$ by step 3. The hypotheses of [def-sc-pic0] are exactly a proper smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field; they now hold, so its degree and kernel-of-degree conventions apply.

source.place: Final paragraph: proper smooth connected geometric curve, agreement of genera, and applicability of the degree/Pic^0 conventions.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A *geometrically integral smooth projective curve
over $k$* is a scheme $C$ over $k$ which is
smooth and projective over $k$
and geometrically integral over
$k$. Its *genus* is

$$
g(C):=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C).
$$

The genus is finite, and it is invariant under base change:
$g(C_{k'})=g(C)$ for every field extension $k'/k$.

For an algebraically
closed extension $k'/k$ the base change $C_{k'}$ is a
proper smooth connected curve in the sense of the
algebraically closed conventions of the smooth-curve chapter, and
$g(C)=g(C_{k'})$ with the genus of [def-sc-genus]; in particular the
degree and $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ conventions of [def-sc-pic0] apply to
$C_{k'}$.

proof.text:
The genus is finite because coherent cohomology of a proper scheme over a
field is finite-dimensional. It is invariant under base change,
$g(C_{k'})=g(C)$, by flat base change along the base change
$C_{k'}\to C$ of [def-pc-base-change].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q131-e2dcde28a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The added dimension-one hypothesis is a justified correction and is reported under 'Statement corrected'. Both source texts, master order 463 and main-20261015 order 469, say only 'a scheme smooth, projective, geometrically integral'. With that wording P^2_k or Spec k (k algebraically closed, K=k) makes the final clause false, because C_K is then not a connected curve in the sense of def-sc-curves. The new wording matches the title, the unit sk-def-av-jacobian ('smooth projective geometrically integral curve'), and both citers, def-sc-jacobian and lem-sc-jacobian-unique, neither of which breaks. All source conclusions are kept, so the target is not weakened. I checked all 6 steps against the cited statements. Step 1: geometric integrality gives geometric irreducibility via def-pc-integral-scheme, so lem-pc-genus-well-defined applies over any k. Step 2: lem-pc-projective-proper gives properness, a field extension is free hence flat, and lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent applies; Stacks 02KH (coherent.tex lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology) shows this isomorphism is linear over the new field. Step 3: pullback of the structure sheaf gives O_{C_K}, then lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change gives the dimensions. Step 4: smoothness, projectivity, dimension 1 (lem-pc-dim-base-change), integrality, and separatedness and finite type from properness. Step 5: (C_K)_L is C_L by def-pc-base-change; this step is genuinely elementary. Step 6: lem-pc-curves-are-sc plus def-sc-genus and def-sc-pic0. No cycle; proof_deps is the union of the step uses. I tested K=k, P^1, an elliptic curve, a pointless conic, and inseparable K. No new nodes. lem-pc-genus-base-change overlaps but carries an extra H^0=k hypothesis, so it is not a duplicate. I accept the 6 declared tool_uses as generic black boxes. Batch-5 flag on lem-pc-genus-well-defined: its closure reaches sec-poincare-duality only through def-pod-ring-scalar-extension (a general definition of scalar extension) and lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change (generic stability under base change). Neither is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality; the lemma is genus finiteness. Accepted. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit, and the uses_not_cited field is stale; both are harmless.
